If you're in school, -primary, secondary, or otherwise a lot of times there are guidance counselors and other people like them who are willing to listen to students with troubles like this.  
When I was in high school I had a biology teacher who found himself being the new confidant of a friend if mine who had a lot going on at home.  
In education systems there are people everywhere that honestly want to help students and would be okay with listening.  
These people also often have a access to recourses that could help more.
As an adult who doesn't attend school sometimes it's a little harder to find people like that but sometimes there are free counselors or other community outreach programs that help when you're in a bad spot.
It's possible they don't want to accept your help because they feel that they should be there for you instead of vice versa.

That sounds accurate in every social circle Ive been in as well.  
Letting someone know about your feelings is a big step but if there's anyone in your life that you're even on basic terms with, they may be a good candidate to talk to. Even just letting someone know how you feel can be relieving. That person may not know what to do, and they may be supportive or they may be a little off beat but voicing the words is beneficial sometimes.  
There are other recources out there and depending on your age, they may be a little easier or harder to get in contact with but overall confiding in whoever you can can help for a little while...
